points.why: Names tragedy-of-the-commons shape with teams each rationally over-claiming the shared queue/GPUs.
Explains restraint is punished as a unilateral loss, fails even when everyone understands, and the people aren't the problem.
Recommends per-team caps, fair-share accounting, visible dashboards, and rules agreed by team leads for enforcement.

pitfalls.why: Explicitly says to stop asking people to behave differently.
Raises capacity only as something to check, noting scheduling changes matter regardless.
